boot-entry only creates a new kernel-boot directory and copies root members once; an existing directory causes refusal. Root replacements do not update its existing copies or a running shell. Old boot state must remain intact.

Init condition targets boot-entry and service has once=1. The reviewed configuration does not make a desktop click or a root file replacement a guardian restart trigger. No accepted same-boot reactivation path is established here.

Even the copied entry sources config-common, which reads fixed ROOT startup.expected/startup.env and root members, while entry executes/checks its HERE boot copies. Both chains must match. Fresh boot alone does not bypass disabled authority, any stop, decoder validation or existing socket refusal.
